learning_outcomes.text: Be able to organize teamwork for vibration analysis in machines within a set timeframe.
Be able to solve simple problems of dynamic behavior of machines using simple mathematical models, CAE tools and/or experimental vibration measurement.
Know how to use CAE computer resources for dynamic analysis of machines.
Use basic technical terminology of vibrations correctly, in English.
Be able to analyze the dynamic behavior of other machines based on previously solved analyses.
Be able to analyze and design machines and machine elements from the point of view of their dynamic behavior.
Be able to obtain suitable models for solving dynamic problems of simple mechanical systems.
Be able to explain vibration control techniques and be able to select and size the most appropriate passive dissipation elements.
Be able to explain the main approximate methods for solving continuous system vibration problems.
Be able to apply vibration measurement techniques in machines and users, and interpret said measurements.
Be able to solve the equations governing the dynamic behavior of simple mechanical systems.
Be able to describe the phenomenon of vibrations and explain its effect on machines and on humans.

syllabus_topics: 1.1. What are vibrations and what is their importance?
1.2. Models for the study of vibrations
2. Vibration of single degree of freedom systems
3. Vibration of N degree of freedom systems
4. Vibration of continuous systems. Approximate methods
4.1. Axial and torsional vibration in bars and shafts
4.4. Approximation methods by discretization. The finite element technique
1. Introduction to vibration measurement: free vibration in 1-DOF systems.
3. Vibration in N-DOF systems: free and forced vibration. FRF.
4. Vibration in continuous systems. The finite element technique. Temporal dynamic analysis.
5. Vibration in continuous systems. The finite element technique. Dynamic analysis in the frequency domain.
teaching_methods: Master class: Exposing theoretical foundations, with multimedia presentations and blackboard support; emphasis on important aspects, doubt resolution, and interactive questioning.
Flipped classroom: Students access theoretical content (videos, presentations, books) outside the classroom and apply knowledge in practical activities in class with instructor assistance.

Exercise and problem solving: Instructor intercalates simple problem solving, emphasizing modeling and calculation. Students solve problems in groups in class, discussing results. Autonomous problem-solving with tutorials.
Laboratory work: Practical teachings using CAE tools for vibration analysis in computer labs and performing vibration measurements on mechanical systems in a laboratory setting.
Project-based learning: Group work assigned to foster self-learning and teamwork, contributing to continuous assessment. Individual tutorials are available throughout the course.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment: Written theoretical-practical knowledge tests
Final exam (Extraordinary call for completion of studies)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a global score of at least 5 out of 10 is required. In the first call, a minimum of 4.5 points out of 10 is required for the exam component; if this is not met, the global average cannot exceed 4.5 points. For the second call, the exam represents 70% (40% exam + 30% from continuous assessment written tests) with a minimum of 4.5 points, while laboratory practices (30%) are non-recoverable. Fraud in any continuous assessment activity typically results in a 0 for that activity, and fraud in the final exam results in a 0 for that call.
